title: Deuteronomy 1: The Second Giving of the Law
body:
Read the chapter → [Deuteronomy 1](/bible/deuteronomy/1)

## Introduction

This session covered Numbers 35-36 together with Deuteronomy 1-2; the Numbers chapters sit in their own chapter set. Deuteronomy means the second giving of the law: the book is a great recapping and reiterating of what already took place, primarily in the book of Numbers, and the audience of the whole book is the Israelites. Chapter 1 retells the order set among the judges and the rebellion at Kadesh-barnea; chapter 2 retells the passage by Esau, Moab, and Ammon, the giants that fell before them, and the destruction of Sihon king of the Amorites.

**[Deuteronomy 1:1-3](/bible/deuteronomy/1#v1)**

> <sup>[1](/bible/deuteronomy/1#v1)</sup> These be the words which Moses spake unto all Israel on this side Jordan in the wilderness, in the plain over against the Red sea, between Paran, and Tophel, and Laban, and Hazeroth, and Dizahab.
>
> <sup>[2](/bible/deuteronomy/1#v2)</sup> (There are eleven days’ journey from Horeb by the way of mount Seir unto Kadesh–barnea.)
>
> <sup>[3](/bible/deuteronomy/1#v3)</sup> And it came to pass in the fortieth year, in the eleventh month, on the first day of the month, that Moses spake unto the children of Israel, according unto all that the Lord had given him in commandment unto them;

- These be the words which Moses spake unto all Israel on this side Jordan in the wilderness: the audience of the entire book of Deuteronomy is the Israelites.
- Moses spake in the fortieth year, in the eleventh month, on the first day of the month, according unto all that the Lord had given him in commandment unto them.

**[Deuteronomy 1:4](/bible/deuteronomy/1#v4)**

> <sup>[4](/bible/deuteronomy/1#v4)</sup> After he had slain Sihon the king of the Amorites, which dwelt in Heshbon, and Og the king of Bashan, which dwelt at Astaroth in Edrei:

- Moses declares this law after he had slain Sihon the king of the Amorites. When the Lord told Abraham his seed would serve four hundred years, he set the time of the return by the Amorites: the iniquity of the Amorites is not yet full.
- By this point their iniquity was fulfilled, like Babylon whose sins reached unto heaven, so the Lord loosed Israel to come through the land of the Amorites and slay Sihon their king.

  Precepts:
  - **[Genesis 15:16](/bible/genesis/15#v16)**
    > <sup>[16](/bible/genesis/15#v16)</sup> But in the fourth generation they shall come hither again: for the iniquity of the Amorites is not yet full.

    The fourth generation would come hither again, for the iniquity of the Amorites was not yet full; Sihon fell when it was full.

**[Deuteronomy 1:5-8](/bible/deuteronomy/1#v5)**

> <sup>[5](/bible/deuteronomy/1#v5)</sup> On this side Jordan, in the land of Moab, began Moses to declare this law, saying,
>
> <sup>[6](/bible/deuteronomy/1#v6)</sup> The Lord our God spake unto us in Horeb, saying, Ye have dwelt long enough in this mount:
>
> <sup>[7](/bible/deuteronomy/1#v7)</sup> Turn you, and take your journey, and go to the mount of the Amorites, and unto all the places nigh thereunto, in the plain, in the hills, and in the vale, and in the south, and by the sea side, to the land of the Canaanites, and unto Lebanon, unto the great river, the river Euphrates.
>
> <sup>[8](/bible/deuteronomy/1#v8)</sup> Behold, I have set the land before you: go in and possess the land which the Lord sware unto your fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, to give unto them and to their seed after them.

- Ye have dwelt long enough in this mount: the Lord set the land before them, from the mount of the Amorites to Lebanon and the great river Euphrates, to go in and possess it.
- The land was sworn unto Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob and to their seed after them; the Most High reiterated that covenant to the fathers over and over through Genesis, reassuring them that their seed would possess the land of Canaan.
- Israel entered not for their own righteousness but for the sake of the promise made to the fathers; the rebellious generation was cut off, yet their children were still brought in because the Most High sware it.

**[Deuteronomy 1:9-12](/bible/deuteronomy/1#v9)**

> <sup>[9](/bible/deuteronomy/1#v9)</sup> And I spake unto you at that time, saying, I am not able to bear you myself alone:
>
> <sup>[10](/bible/deuteronomy/1#v10)</sup> The Lord your God hath multiplied you, and, behold, ye are this day as the stars of heaven for multitude.
>
> <sup>[11](/bible/deuteronomy/1#v11)</sup> (The Lord God of your fathers make you a thousand times so many more as ye are, and bless you, as he hath promised you!)
>
> <sup>[12](/bible/deuteronomy/1#v12)</sup> How can I myself alone bear your cumbrance, and your burden, and your strife?

- I am not able to bear you myself alone: the people were multiplied as the stars of heaven, and every one of them came with cumbrance, burden, and strife.
- Moses refers back to what his father in law saw in Exodus 18: Moses sat judging the people alone from morning until evening, the people waiting all day in line, because they came to him to inquire of God and be shown the statutes and laws.
- His father in law told him the thing was not good: judging alone would wear away both Moses and the people. The counsel was to provide able men that fear God and set them in ranks over thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens.

  Precepts:
  - **[Exodus 18:17-18](/bible/exodus/18#v17)**
    > <sup>[17](/bible/exodus/18#v17)</sup> And Moses’ father in law said unto him, The thing that thou doest is not good.
    >
    > <sup>[18](/bible/exodus/18#v18)</sup> Thou wilt surely wear away, both thou, and this people that is with thee: for this thing is too heavy for thee; thou art not able to perform it thyself alone.

    The thing that thou doest is not good; thou wilt surely wear away, both thou and this people, for the thing is too heavy for one man.
  - **[Exodus 18:21](/bible/exodus/18#v21)**
    > <sup>[21](/bible/exodus/18#v21)</sup> Moreover thou shalt provide out of all the people able men, such as fear God, men of truth, hating covetousness; and place such over them, to be rulers of thousands, and rulers of hundreds, rulers of fifties, and rulers of tens:

    Provide able men, such as fear God, men of truth, hating covetousness, and place them as rulers of thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens.

**[Deuteronomy 1:13-15](/bible/deuteronomy/1#v13)**

> <sup>[13](/bible/deuteronomy/1#v13)</sup> Take you wise men, and understanding, and known among your tribes, and I will make them rulers over you.
>
> <sup>[14](/bible/deuteronomy/1#v14)</sup> And ye answered me, and said, The thing which thou hast spoken is good for us to do.
>
> <sup>[15](/bible/deuteronomy/1#v15)</sup> So I took the chief of your tribes, wise men, and known, and made them heads over you, captains over thousands, and captains over hundreds, and captains over fifties, and captains over tens, and officers among your tribes.

- The people answered that the thing was good to do, and Moses took the chief of the tribes, wise men and known, and made them captains over thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens, and officers among the tribes.
- Rank in a congregation is biblical. With schools worldwide, every issue cannot come to one man; soldiers, officers, captains, deacons, and bishop follow the same order the fathers ordained here, and the terminology of this verse is the terminology used in the body today.

**[Deuteronomy 1:16-18](/bible/deuteronomy/1#v16)**

> <sup>[16](/bible/deuteronomy/1#v16)</sup> And I charged your judges at that time, saying, Hear the causes between your brethren, and judge righteously between every man and his brother, and the stranger that is with him.
>
> <sup>[17](/bible/deuteronomy/1#v17)</sup> Ye shall not respect persons in judgment; but ye shall hear the small as well as the great; ye shall not be afraid of the face of man; for the judgment is God’s: and the cause that is too hard for you, bring it unto me, and I will hear it.
>
> <sup>[18](/bible/deuteronomy/1#v18)</sup> And I commanded you at that time all the things which ye should do.

- The charge to the judges: hear the causes between brethren and judge righteously between every man and his brother and the stranger with him, and hear the small as well as the great.
- Ye shall not respect persons in judgment: a poor man gets no pass for being poor, and a mighty man with money and possessions is not above the laws of the Most High; no one can buy himself out of judgment.
- Ye shall not be afraid of the face of man, for the judgment is God's: no tough face may intimidate or sway a verdict, because it is the Most High passing the judgment through the judge. The cause too hard goes up the chain to Moses, and that chain itself was instituted here.

  Precepts:
  - **[Leviticus 19:15](/bible/leviticus/19#v15)**
    > <sup>[15](/bible/leviticus/19#v15)</sup> Ye shall do no unrighteousness in judgment: thou shalt not respect the person of the poor, nor honour the person of the mighty: but in righteousness shalt thou judge thy neighbour.

    Do no unrighteousness in judgment; respect not the person of the poor, nor honour the person of the mighty.

**[Deuteronomy 1:19-25](/bible/deuteronomy/1#v19)**

> <sup>[19](/bible/deuteronomy/1#v19)</sup> And when we departed from Horeb, we went through all that great and terrible wilderness, which ye saw by the way of the mountain of the Amorites, as the Lord our God commanded us; and we came to Kadesh–barnea.
>
> <sup>[20](/bible/deuteronomy/1#v20)</sup> And I said unto you, Ye are come unto the mountain of the Amorites, which the Lord our God doth give unto us.
>
> <sup>[21](/bible/deuteronomy/1#v21)</sup> Behold, the Lord thy God hath set the land before thee: go up and possess it, as the Lord God of thy fathers hath said unto thee; fear not, neither be discouraged.
>
> <sup>[22](/bible/deuteronomy/1#v22)</sup> And ye came near unto me every one of you, and said, We will send men before us, and they shall search us out the land, and bring us word again by what way we must go up, and into what cities we shall come.
>
> <sup>[23](/bible/deuteronomy/1#v23)</sup> And the saying pleased me well: and I took twelve men of you, one of a tribe:
>
> <sup>[24](/bible/deuteronomy/1#v24)</sup> And they turned and went up into the mountain, and came unto the valley of Eshcol, and searched it out.
>
> <sup>[25](/bible/deuteronomy/1#v25)</sup> And they took of the fruit of the land in their hands, and brought it down unto us, and brought us word again, and said, It is a good land which the Lord our God doth give us.

- Israel came through that great and terrible wilderness to Kadesh-barnea, to the mountain of the Amorites, and the commandment was plain: the Lord hath set the land before thee; go up and possess it; fear not, neither be discouraged.
- The people asked to send men first to search out the land and bring word of the way and the cities, and the saying pleased Moses; twelve men, one of a tribe, went up to the valley of Eshcol.
- The spies brought of the fruit of the land in their hands and brought word again: it is a good land which the Lord our God doth give us.

**[Deuteronomy 1:26-28](/bible/deuteronomy/1#v26)**

> <sup>[26](/bible/deuteronomy/1#v26)</sup> Notwithstanding ye would not go up, but rebelled against the commandment of the Lord your God:
>
> <sup>[27](/bible/deuteronomy/1#v27)</sup> And ye murmured in your tents, and said, Because the Lord hated us, he hath brought us forth out of the land of Egypt, to deliver us into the hand of the Amorites, to destroy us.
>
> <sup>[28](/bible/deuteronomy/1#v28)</sup> Whither shall we go up? our brethren have discouraged our heart, saying, The people is greater and taller than we; the cities are great and walled up to heaven; and moreover we have seen the sons of the Anakims there.

- Notwithstanding ye would not go up, but rebelled against the commandment of the Lord: they acknowledged the land was good, yet all refused except Caleb and Joshua, who had faith to go take it.
- They murmured in their tents that the Lord hated them and brought them out of Egypt to deliver them into the hand of the Amorites to destroy them.
- The spies had discouraged their hearts with the report: the people greater and taller than we, cities great and walled up to heaven, and the sons of the Anakims, the giants, in the land.

**[Deuteronomy 1:29-31](/bible/deuteronomy/1#v29)**

> <sup>[29](/bible/deuteronomy/1#v29)</sup> Then I said unto you, Dread not, neither be afraid of them.
>
> <sup>[30](/bible/deuteronomy/1#v30)</sup> The Lord your God which goeth before you, he shall fight for you, according to all that he did for you in Egypt before your eyes;
>
> <sup>[31](/bible/deuteronomy/1#v31)</sup> And in the wilderness, where thou hast seen how that the Lord thy God bare thee, as a man doth bear his son, in all the way that ye went, until ye came into this place.

- Dread not, neither be afraid of them: the Lord your God which goeth before you, he shall fight for you, according to all that he did in Egypt before your eyes.
- The Amorites were no mightier than Egypt, and these same Israelites witnessed how the Lord broke Egypt to bring them out; where was their faith?
- The principle still applies: the body still has adversaries that rise against it, and the command remains to be in nothing terrified by them. Fear of the adversary is a spirit the Most High never gave his people; whoever is terrified of the enemy is out of the Spirit.

  Precepts:
  - **[Philippians 1:28](/bible/philippians/1#v28)**
    > <sup>[28](/bible/philippians/1#v28)</sup> And in nothing terrified by your adversaries: which is to them an evident token of perdition, but to you of salvation, and that of God.

    In nothing terrified by your adversaries, which is to them an evident token of perdition, but to you of salvation, and that of God.
  - **[2 Timothy 1:7](/bible/2-timothy/1#v7)**
    > <sup>[7](/bible/2-timothy/1#v7)</sup> For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.

    God hath not given us the spirit of fear, but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.

**[Deuteronomy 1:32-33](/bible/deuteronomy/1#v32)**

> <sup>[32](/bible/deuteronomy/1#v32)</sup> Yet in this thing ye did not believe the Lord your God,
>
> <sup>[33](/bible/deuteronomy/1#v33)</sup> Who went in the way before you, to search you out a place to pitch your tents in, in fire by night, to shew you by what way ye should go, and in a cloud by day.

- The Lord bare Israel in the wilderness as a man doth bear his son, went before them in fire by night and in a cloud by day to search out a place to pitch their tents; yet in this thing ye did not believe the Lord your God.
- That is the amazing part of this history: they saw all the miracles and were carried like a son, and still believed the Lord was setting them up to be killed by giants, when a giant has nothing on the Most High.
- The fathers in the wilderness had the gospel preached to them as we have: deliverance from captivity into the promised kingdom. But the word did not profit them, not being mixed with faith; they had the laws without the faith, and it is impossible to have one without the other.

  Precepts:
  - **[Hebrews 4:1-2](/bible/hebrews/4#v1)**
    > <sup>[1](/bible/hebrews/4#v1)</sup> Let us therefore fear, lest, a promise being left us of entering into his rest, any of you should seem to come short of it.
    >
    > <sup>[2](/bible/hebrews/4#v2)</sup> For unto us was the gospel preached, as well as unto them: but the word preached did not profit them, not being mixed with faith in them that heard it.

    Fear lest ye come short as the fathers did: the gospel was preached unto them as unto us, but the word did not profit them, not being mixed with faith in them that heard it.
  - **[Revelation 14:12](/bible/revelation/14#v12)**
    > <sup>[12](/bible/revelation/14#v12)</sup> Here is the patience of the saints: here are they that keep the commandments of God, and the faith of Jesus.

    The saints keep the commandments of God and the faith of Jesus; commandments and faith go together.

**[Deuteronomy 1:34-38](/bible/deuteronomy/1#v34)**

> <sup>[34](/bible/deuteronomy/1#v34)</sup> And the Lord heard the voice of your words, and was wroth, and sware, saying,
>
> <sup>[35](/bible/deuteronomy/1#v35)</sup> Surely there shall not one of these men of this evil generation see that good land, which I sware to give unto your fathers,
>
> <sup>[36](/bible/deuteronomy/1#v36)</sup> Save Caleb the son of Jephunneh; he shall see it, and to him will I give the land that he hath trodden upon, and to his children, because he hath wholly followed the Lord.
>
> <sup>[37](/bible/deuteronomy/1#v37)</sup> Also the Lord was angry with me for your sakes, saying, Thou also shalt not go in thither.
>
> <sup>[38](/bible/deuteronomy/1#v38)</sup> But Joshua the son of Nun, which standeth before thee, he shall go in thither: encourage him: for he shall cause Israel to inherit it.

- The Lord heard their words and was wroth and sware: not one of the men of that evil generation would see the good land, save Caleb the son of Jephunneh, because he wholly followed the Lord, and Joshua the son of Nun, who would cause Israel to inherit it.
- Also the Lord was angry with me for your sakes: at the waters the people fell into the same disbelief they had shown over and over, and Moses in his anger called them rebels and smote the rock twice when the Lord had said to speak to the rock.
- Anger lets the commandments slip: be angry and sin not, but when anger takes hold, a man fails to apply what he knows, and Moses failed to sanctify the Most High in the eyes of the children of Israel. His judgment was to be kept out of the land.
- Moses is still good; he stood with Elias before Christ on the mount. He missed the promised land at that time, not the kingdom. But leadership carries the greater condemnation: the more given unto you, the more stripes when you fail.

  Precepts:
  - **[Numbers 20:8-12](/bible/numbers/20#v8)**
    > <sup>[8](/bible/numbers/20#v8)</sup> Take the rod, and gather thou the assembly together, thou, and Aaron thy brother, and speak ye unto the rock before their eyes; and it shall give forth his water, and thou shalt bring forth to them water out of the rock: so thou shalt give the congregation and their beasts drink.
    >
    > <sup>[9](/bible/numbers/20#v9)</sup> And Moses took the rod from before the Lord, as he commanded him.
    >
    > <sup>[10](/bible/numbers/20#v10)</sup> And Moses and Aaron gathered the congregation together before the rock, and he said unto them, Hear now, ye rebels; must we fetch you water out of this rock?
    >
    > <sup>[11](/bible/numbers/20#v11)</sup> And Moses lifted up his hand, and with his rod he smote the rock twice: and the water came out abundantly, and the congregation drank, and their beasts also.
    >
    > <sup>[12](/bible/numbers/20#v12)</sup> And the Lord spake unto Moses and Aaron, Because ye believed me not, to sanctify me in the eyes of the children of Israel, therefore ye shall not bring this congregation into the land which I have given them.

    The Lord said speak ye unto the rock; Moses smote it twice in anger, and because he believed not, to sanctify the Lord in the eyes of Israel, he could not bring the congregation into the land.
  - **[Ephesians 4:26](/bible/ephesians/4#v26)**
    > <sup>[26](/bible/ephesians/4#v26)</sup> Be ye angry, and sin not: let not the sun go down upon your wrath:

    Be ye angry, and sin not; anger given room makes a man cast the commandments aside.
  - **[Matthew 17:3](/bible/matthew/17#v3)**
    > <sup>[3](/bible/matthew/17#v3)</sup> And, behold, there appeared unto them Moses and Elias talking with him.

    Moses and Elias appeared talking with Christ on the mount; Moses is good.

**[Deuteronomy 1:39-40](/bible/deuteronomy/1#v39)**

> <sup>[39](/bible/deuteronomy/1#v39)</sup> Moreover your little ones, which ye said should be a prey, and your children, which in that day had no knowledge between good and evil, they shall go in thither, and unto them will I give it, and they shall possess it.
>
> <sup>[40](/bible/deuteronomy/1#v40)</sup> But as for you, turn you, and take your journey into the wilderness by the way of the Red sea.

- The little ones, the children which in that day had no knowledge between good and evil, would go in and possess the land the Most High sware to the fathers.
- As for that generation, the command was to turn and take their journey into the wilderness by the way of the Red sea.

**[Deuteronomy 1:41-46](/bible/deuteronomy/1#v41)**

> <sup>[41](/bible/deuteronomy/1#v41)</sup> Then ye answered and said unto me, We have sinned against the Lord, we will go up and fight, according to all that the Lord our God commanded us. And when ye had girded on every man his weapons of war, ye were ready to go up into the hill.
>
> <sup>[42](/bible/deuteronomy/1#v42)</sup> And the Lord said unto me, Say unto them, Go not up, neither fight; for I am not among you; lest ye be smitten before your enemies.
>
> <sup>[43](/bible/deuteronomy/1#v43)</sup> So I spake unto you; and ye would not hear, but rebelled against the commandment of the Lord, and went presumptuously up into the hill.
>
> <sup>[44](/bible/deuteronomy/1#v44)</sup> And the Amorites, which dwelt in that mountain, came out against you, and chased you, as bees do, and destroyed you in Seir, even unto Hormah.
>
> <sup>[45](/bible/deuteronomy/1#v45)</sup> And ye returned and wept before the Lord; but the Lord would not hearken to your voice, nor give ear unto you.
>
> <sup>[46](/bible/deuteronomy/1#v46)</sup> So ye abode in Kadesh many days, according unto the days that ye abode there.

- Then ye answered, We have sinned: only after the judgment fell did they want to repent, girding on weapons of war and declaring themselves ready to go up. The Lord had given chance after chance to obey and not fear, and every time the same trial brought the same unbelief; do nothing without advice, and when thou hast once done, repent not.
- The Lord said go not up, neither fight, for I am not among you, lest ye be smitten before your enemies; and they went up presumptuously anyway, boldly doing what they were told not to do, as recorded in [Numbers 14](/bible/numbers/14).
- The Amorites came out against them and chased them as bees do, and destroyed them in Seir unto Hormah.
- They returned and wept before the Lord, but the Lord would not hearken to their voice nor give ear. When counsel is set at nought until the judgment lands, the weeping comes too late; they that hated knowledge and did not choose the fear of the Lord seek him early and do not find him. So they abode in Kadesh many days.

  Precepts:
  - **[Proverbs 1:25-29](/bible/proverbs/1#v25)**
    > <sup>[25](/bible/proverbs/1#v25)</sup> But ye have set at nought all my counsel, and would none of my reproof:
    >
    > <sup>[26](/bible/proverbs/1#v26)</sup> I also will laugh at your calamity; I will mock when your fear cometh;
    >
    > <sup>[27](/bible/proverbs/1#v27)</sup> When your fear cometh as desolation, and your destruction cometh as a whirlwind; when distress and anguish cometh upon you.
    >
    > <sup>[28](/bible/proverbs/1#v28)</sup> Then shall they call upon me, but I will not answer; they shall seek me early, but they shall not find me:
    >
    > <sup>[29](/bible/proverbs/1#v29)</sup> For that they hated knowledge, and did not choose the fear of the Lord:

    They set at nought all his counsel and would none of his reproof; when the fear comes he laughs at the calamity, and they that call then are not answered, for they hated knowledge.
  - **[Ecclesiasticus 32:19](/bible/sirach/32#v19)**
    > <sup>[19](/bible/sirach/32#v19)</sup> Do nothing without advice; and when thou hast once done, repent not.

    Once the judgment is done, the apology does not undo it; the counsel had to be taken beforehand.
